# `promiseAllInEffect`

Warns when Promise.all or Promise.allSettled fans out over an array inside Effect code instead of Effect.forEach or Effect.all with a concurrency option

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Category | Effect-native |
| Default severity | `off` |
| Fixable | Yes |
| Effect versions | v3, v4 |
| Diagnostic codes | `TS377198` |
| Language Service name | `promiseAllInEffect` |
| Oxlint name | `effecttsgo/promise-all-in-effect` |

## Preview

```ts
import { Effect } from "effect"

declare const ids: ReadonlyArray<string>
declare const fetchUser: (id: string) => Promise<{ readonly name: string }>

export const users = Effect.tryPromise(() => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))
/**
                                             ^^^^^^^^^^^ effecttsgo(promise-all-in-effect): `Promise.all` starts every promise at once with no concurrency bound, and they keep running when the fiber is interrupted. Use `Effect.forEach` with a concurrency option instead.
*/
```

```jsonc
      }

}
```
